narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: close enough to see water physically leaving stone, and framed so the absence of anything above the rock is unmistakable. The reader must feel the mass-balance problem before any physics arrives.
subject: A close view of the underside of a floating mountain: dark, wet, deeply fractured rock filling the upper part of the frame, and from a single seam near its lowest point a thick ribbon of white water walking out of the stone into open air. The water holds together for a stretch, then frays and comes apart into a drifting veil of faintly glowing spray. Beyond and below is nothing but hazy open air. No land is visible above the rock anywhere in the frame.
scene: Directly beneath a suspended massif, kilometres of empty air below, thin cloud drifting past the rock face.
camera: Close three-quarter view looking up at the underside, the rock overhead and the falling water leading the eye down out of frame.
light: Strong backlight from off-frame, so the falling water and its spray glow bright while the rock face stays dark and textural.
palette: Dark cool grey-violet wet rock, bright misty-cyan water and spray, deep void-indigo hazy air beyond, a faint teal glow where mist catches bioluminescence.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, hand-painted, wet rock rendered with real texture, soft atmospheric spray, NOT a photograph and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: High on the seam where water leaves the stone and on the fractured rock texture around it; softening rapidly into haze away from the water.
composition: Rock mass across the top and one side, the water emerging near the centre and falling out of frame, and a large area of plain dark hazy air on the opposite side kept clear for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: Same wet grey-violet rock and glowing cyan water as the cover, seen much closer. Leave one side of the frame plain and dark for annotation callouts.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no terrain visible above the rock
